independent_acceptance.reasoning: For a fixed PSL2(R)^2, a,b in Gamma(2)/?I freely generate by ping-pong and both displace i by arcosh(3). Product with arithmetic quaternion Fuchsian lattices of unbounded totally real adjoint trace degree has that degree as the product trace field; the radius eventually includes both fixed generators. A virtually nilpotent group cannot contain F2. The unrestricted Theorem C fails, while irreducible Theorem 3.1 is not refuted.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: Factorwise nonelliptic radii ignore projected torsion. Every nonidentity element of torsion-free Gamma has an infinite-order projection; inverse radius power is bounded by the sum of factor powers. Normalized finite-cover integration cancels its arbitrary index. For disconnected effective groups gamma^f lies in Gamma0 and is nonidentity, giving epsilon_Gamma>=epsilon_Gamma0/f and a uniform f^n factor. This completion is valid conditional on the named standard arithmetic-lattice decomposition.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The actual body theorem imposes irreducibility. The rational-structure objection was withdrawn; no reinstatement without proof.

problems.title: Invalid rank-one spectral computation and compact-factor orbital scope
problems.claim: Criticalexponentsm,m,2m andboundarydimensionformula yieldpositiveuniformgap; everysemisimpleGfinitecenter allows exponentialorbitalgrowth.
problems.assumptions: SO0(2,1), centralizerSO0(1,1), cyclicuniformlattice; separatelyG0×SO3 withΓ0×finite nonabelian tetrahedralgroup andγnoncentralinboth.
problems.correction: Useentropyh=2||rho|| withcorrect subgroupgrowth andeffective noncompactscope; chooseconvolutionsquare. CorrectCS/support/iterationthenchecked.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: A cyclic uniform lattice in SO0(1,1) has linear orbit growth and critical exponent zero. The printed m=1 gives lambda0=0 in the displayed formula, contradicting the claimed gap. Entropy 2||rho||, not topological boundary dimension, gives the correct rank-one parameter. For G0?SO3, gamma=(1,u) with u noncentral in the tetrahedral group and SO3 has positive constant compact-orbit mass at all positive radii, so the broad orbital-growth assertion fails. Here noncentrality is in those compact groups, not in the trivial G0 projection.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: The corrected real and complex subgroup entropies give a positive gap in the effective noncompact scope. Convolution-square positivity, support enlargement R to R+2, integral preservation, Cauchy?Schwarz and iteration recover the intended orbital estimate. This does not validate the original calculation.
independent_acceptance.dependency: Uniform gap -> orbital growth -> thin-volume estimate -> core complexity argument. The local no-compact-factor statement on p5 is explicitly scoped to its paragraph; it does not silently repair the separately stated theorem.

problems.title: False splitting-field dimension bound in height comparison
problems.claim: Commonadjointroot-value field hasdegree<=dimG; unweighted archimedeansum boundsprintedheight.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: For t^5-t-1, reduction modulo 3 has no linear or irreducible quadratic divisor, hence is irreducible; modulo 2 it factors as the stated irreducible quadratic times cubic. The primitive degree-five Galois group contains a transposition and is S5. Fixing all root ratios scales every root by one scalar; nonzero fourth and fifth elementary symmetric functions force that scalar to be 1. Thus the root-value field has degree120>dim(PGL5)=24.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: Root-value multiset Galois invariance cancels [L:k] in the Weil-height sum. The exact real-plus-twice-complex-place formula yields S<=d*h<=2S and the intended comparison, including a multiplicative zero-height formulation. The individual eigenvalue-degree bound used in Dobrowolski remains valid. No new numerical execution was needed.

problems.title: Missing multiplicative constant in overlap bound

independent_acceptance.reasoning: The degree-one uniform arithmetic SO+(x1?+x2?+x3??7x4?,Z) is anisotropic by the mod8/descent argument. The order-four rotation and its square give two distinct positive-radius tubes through their common axis, refuting the exact bound1. The initial proof already produces multiplicative constants, so this is a local boundary defect rather than a refutation of the polynomial scale.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: Retain C(d+1)^m. Semisimplicity follows from semisimple powers in characteristic zero. Select the invariant flat via the transverse finite-group fixed point in Min(L0); finite kernel and root-of-unity/Jordan bounds remain named external inputs. Lift translation lengths equal projected lengths by equivariant nearest-point projection. Successive-minima vectors need not form a basis (index-two four-dimensional example); direct separated coset packing A(r)(1+2R/ell)^r covers all radii, with rank zero and bounded degree treated separately.

problems.title: Nonuniform tube-volume class sum diverges
problems.check: Centralizer=<tau>; exacttubearea2sinh(R/2)/j; gcdmatrixentryconjugacyinvariant distinguishesclasses; harmonicdivergence whilequotientfinitearea.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: In PSL2(Z), centralizer of z->z+j is generated by z->z+1; the centralizer-quotient tube area is exactly 2sinh(R/2)/j. The gcd invariant of the trace-two matrix representative separates positive powers into distinct classes. Their harmonic class sum diverges for any allowed positive R, while the ambient quotient has finite area.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: Uniformity and the polynomial prefactor restore the needed compact application; first unfold over Gamma\G and normalize K. Standard injectivity radius requires displacement2R. Monotonicity with enlarged constant handles the bounded-degree prefactored estimate, but does not prove the stricter Theorem D fraction.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: Equal radius1/6 balls at distance1/4 intersect while neither center is in the other's ball and the net separation is respected. The printed final count therefore misses legitimate nerve edges. Intersecting balls and the 1-Lipschitz radius give s<2epsilon_p/5, epsilon_q>3epsilon_p/5, and neighbor separation epsilon_p/60, hence C_X(49) and the corresponding incident-simplex bound.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: The correct lifted packing uses disjoint eta/2 balls in radius delta+eta/2, giving C_X(2delta/eta+1). The two-point H2 rational example genuinely violates the printed bound. Integral F_p is the smaller/larger ball-volume ratio, at least1/C_X(2), rather than1; multiplicity becomes C_X(73) and the total count constant C_X(2)^2*C_X(73). Coverage, finite maximality, unique lifts and convex intersections survive, so the full local replacement works.
independent_acceptance.severity_basis: The invalid neighbor count is the final essential bounded-incidence step of Proposition6.1/TheoremA. A verified short repair does not erase that original core derivation error.
